intro: Liechtenstein is a tiny Alpine principality named after the noble family that bought it in the early 1700s. It has had no army since 1868.

chapters.title: A principality
text: The Liechtenstein family bought the lordships of Schellenberg and Vaduz and in 1719 the Holy Roman Emperor made them a principality. It became fully sovereign in 1806.

chapters.title: Neutral and armyless
text: Liechtenstein abolished its army in 1868. According to a popular story, its last 80 soldiers came home from a campaign with 81 men, having made a friend on the way. It stayed neutral in both world wars.

chapters.title: Modern Liechtenstein
text: Since 1923 it has had a customs union with Switzerland and uses the Swiss franc. It joined the United Nations in 1990.

timeline.title: Principality
timeline.text: The emperor creates the Principality of Liechtenstein.

keyTerms.meaning: A state ruled by a prince.
